title: What is the difference between anyMatch(), allMatch(), and noneMatch(), and how does each short-circuit?
shortTitle: anyMatch vs allMatch vs noneMatch — short-circuiting behavior

s1_definition.profdef: All three are short-circuiting terminal operations returning boolean:
s1_definition.analogy: anyMatch = "Is ANY trade above Rs.10L?" → checks one by one, first YES → stops, returns true. allMatch = "Are ALL trades settled?" → checks one by one, first NO → stops, returns false. noneMatch = "Are there NO failed trades?" → checks one by one, first FAILED found → stops, returns false.
s1_definition.oneliner: anyMatch: first true→true. allMatch: first false→false. noneMatch: first true→false. All short-circuit. Empty: anyMatch=false, allMatch=true, noneMatch=true.
s1_definition.raw:
**Professional definition:** All three are short-circuiting terminal operations returning boolean:

| Method | Returns true when | Short-circuits on | Empty stream |
|--------|-------------------|-------------------|-------------|
| `anyMatch(pred)` | ANY element matches | First TRUE → returns true | false |
| `allMatch(pred)` | ALL elements match | First FALSE → returns false | true |
| `noneMatch(pred)` | NO element matches | First TRUE → returns false | true |

**In simple words (banking analogy):** anyMatch = "Is ANY trade above Rs.10L?" → checks one by one, first YES → stops, returns true. allMatch = "Are ALL trades settled?" → checks one by one, first NO → stops, returns false. noneMatch = "Are there NO failed trades?" → checks one by one, first FAILED found → stops, returns false.

**One line to remember:** anyMatch: first true→true. allMatch: first false→false. noneMatch: first true→false. All short-circuit. Empty: anyMatch=false, allMatch=true, noneMatch=true.

sections.s2_technical:
The three matching terminal operations return a boolean and short-circuit. `anyMatch(predicate)` returns true as soon as ONE element satisfies the predicate, then stops — ideal for "is there at least one suspicious transaction". `allMatch(predicate)` returns false as soon as ONE element fails — ideal for "are all accounts active". `noneMatch(predicate)` returns false as soon as ONE element matches — ideal for "are there zero overdrawn accounts".

Short-circuiting means they do not necessarily examine every element, which makes them efficient on large or even infinite streams. Edge cases on an empty stream follow logic: `anyMatch` is false (no element matched), `allMatch` is true (vacuously — nothing violated it), and `noneMatch` is true (nothing matched). These vacuous-truth results surprise people, so test them explicitly.

A banking example: `txns.stream().anyMatch(t -> t.amount().compareTo(LIMIT) > 0)` flags a batch for review the instant a large transfer appears, without scanning the rest. Senior nuance: for existence use `anyMatch`, not `filter(...).count() > 0`, because `anyMatch` stops at the first hit while `count()` consumes the whole stream.
sections.s3_banking: Problem — A compliance check used `filter(...).count() > 0` to detect any large transfer, which scanned every transaction even after the first hit. Fix: `anyMatch` short-circuits and returns true the instant a large transfer is found, while `allMatch`/`noneMatch` cover the "all active" and "none overdrawn" checks efficiently.

sections.s5_journey:
**Step 1.** Input: amounts [5000, 20000, 150000, 3000].

**Step 2.** `anyMatch(a -> a > 100000)` scans 5000, 20000, then 150000 which matches — returns true and stops without checking 3000.

**Step 3.** `allMatch(a -> a > 0)` checks each; all are positive, so true.

**Step 4.** `noneMatch(a -> a < 0)` finds no negative, so true.

**Step 5.** On an empty stream, `allMatch` is vacuously true and `anyMatch` is false.

```text
INFO: any=true all=true none=true (emptyAll=true emptyAny=false)
```
sections.s5b_flow:
```
  ═══ anyMatch — stops on first TRUE ═══
  [1, 2, 3, 4, 5].anyMatch(n → n == 3)
  Check 1 → false. Check 2 → false. Check 3 → TRUE → STOP! Return true.

  ═══ allMatch — stops on first FALSE ═══
  [2, 4, 5, 6, 8].allMatch(n → n%2==0)
  Check 2 → true. Check 4 → true. Check 5 → FALSE → STOP! Return false.

  ═══ noneMatch — stops on first TRUE ═══
  ["OK", "OK", "FAILED"].noneMatch(s → "FAILED")
  Check OK → false. Check OK → false. Check FAILED → TRUE → STOP! Return false.
```

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Match Ops (Banking Fraud / Compliance Short-Circuit)      │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  transactions.stream()                                     │
│        ▼                                                   │
│  anyMatch(Txn::isFlagged)   ─► ANY suspicious? stop @1st T │
│  allMatch(Txn::isCompliant) ─► ALL KYC-ok?    stop @1st F  │

```
sections.s5d_lld:
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Short-circuiting terminal boolean operations            │
│───────────────────────────────────────────────────────── │
│ anyMatch(p):  true on FIRST match      → stops           │
│ allMatch(p):  false on FIRST violation → stops           │
│ noneMatch(p): true on FIRST match      → stops (→false)  │
│ all three stop early → O(k) not O(n) in best case        │
└───────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────── │
                │ empty-stream + identities                 │
                ▼                                            │
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ empty stream: anyMatch=false,                            │
│   allMatch=true (vacuous truth), noneMatch=true          │
│ identity: noneMatch(p) == !anyMatch(p)                   │
│           allMatch(p)  == noneMatch(p.negate())          │
│ Banking: anyMatch(isHighRisk) to trip fraud alert fast;  │
│   allMatch(isKycVerified) as account-open precondition   │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
anyMatch returns true if ANY element matches the predicate — it short-circuits on the first true. allMatch returns true only if ALL elements match — it short-circuits on the first false. noneMatch returns true only if NO element matches — it short-circuits on the first true (same trigger as anyMatch, opposite result). For empty streams: anyMatch returns false (no element matched), allMatch returns true (no element violated — vacuous truth), noneMatch returns true (no element matched). noneMatch(pred) is logically equivalent to !anyMatch(pred).
